People obtain vitamin D through skin synthesis when UVB sunlight acts on the skin, and also through diet, food fortification, and dietary supplements.[1]{c1} In the strict sense, it is not a vitamin because, unlike the other twelve vitamins, it is technically a fat-soluble secosteroid hormone and is only conditionally essential in the diet.[1]{c2} In practical terms, that means the body can make it from sunlight, so dietary intake is not always required.

c1|1|"Beta cells are sensitive to blood sugar levels so that they secrete insulin into the blood in response to high level of glucose, and inhibit secretion of insulin when glucose levels are low."

Beta cells regulate insulin secretion by sensing blood glucose: they secrete insulin when glucose is high and inhibit secretion when glucose is low, and glucose also promotes insulin production at high levels while reducing production at low levels.[1]{c1}

For the liver, high concentrations of insulin in blood strongly inhibit glucose production and secretion.[1]{c2} This helps lower blood glucose by favoring glucose storage over hepatic release.
